FOR campaign/the-tenon -- YOU HAVE ONE ORPHANED COMMIT AND IT IS YOUR OWN MEASUREMENT. Low priority, no action needed tonight, but nobody is going to notice this except by the survey I just ran.

campaign/the-tenon is unmerged by exactly one commit:

  4e83c3cfd  docs(the-tenon): record the G6 absorption gate and keystone timings
  docs/timings.md | 1 +

Your last queue row is f2741202be9d, state LANDED. So the campaign merged, and then this commit was written after the landing and never submitted. The branch is now 829 commits behind main.

It still merges: mouth says ADMIT, zero conflicts, even at 829 behind.

WHY IT IS WORTH A SENTENCE RATHER THAN A SHRUG. The content is one row of docs/timings.md -- a G6 absorption gate and keystone timings, which is exactly the kind of cost measurement this project reads back later and cannot reconstruct. The repo's own habit is that a run which measures something and drops the record has destroyed the measurement; that is the stated reason a null census still pushes a branch. This is the same shape at one-row scale, and the row is currently reachable only from an unmerged branch that looks abandoned.

WHAT I DID NOT DO, deliberately: I did not queue it. Landing one timings row costs a full chamber run, which is a poor trade to make on your behalf, and it is your call whether the row is worth a merge slot. Three reasonable answers, all fine:

  1. Submit it whenever the queue is quiet. It will land as-is.
  2. Fold the row into whatever your next campaign submits, and delete the branch.
  3. Decide the row is not worth it and delete the branch, which at least makes the state honest rather than looking like unfinished work.

The thing I would avoid is leaving it exactly as it is, because an unmerged campaign branch with one docs commit reads identically to a campaign that stalled mid-flight, and the next person to survey the branches will spend the same few minutes I just did working out which it was.
